en: The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the One-Syllable Uṣṇīṣa-Cakravartin King.
Compiled by [Name], Grand Master of the Household with the Rank of Peer of the State, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial,
Duke of Sū, Feudal Lord of Three Thousand Households, Invested with Purple Robes, and Posthumously Honored as Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

Translated by the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra, Tripitaka Master of Daxingshan Monastery, who bears the posthumous title of Great Mirror and the honorary name of Great Universal Wisdom, by Imperial Command. I now rely upon the ritual procedures for the recitation of the Sovereign One-Syllable Uṣṇīṣa-Cakra-Rāja, the supreme among all Buddha-uṣṇīṣas and the highest of mantras—both mundane and supramundane—which possess incomparable power and surpass the world, as taught by the Tathāgata Śākyamuni at the assembly in the Tuṣita Heaven Palace.
The practitioner should first enter this Great Maṇḍala of the King of Uṣṇīṣa Cakras.
Only after receiving the empowerment and authorization of an ācārya should one receive this dharma.
One must first understand this thoroughly and clearly;
thereafter, place the image of the Honored One in a pure location and prostrate with one's head toward the west in salutation.

Having taken the three refuges, surrendered the body, confessed transgressions, received the precepts, generated the bodhicitta, expressed sympathetic joy, made requests, formulated vows, and performed the dedication of merit,
one should then bind the Samaya-mudrā of the Buddha Family.
Interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward,
extend both thumbs side by side, and hold them upright.
It is thus accomplished.
This is called the Heart-Seal Mantra of all Tathāgatas, which says:
Oṃ īna īṃ. Next, one should form the Samaya Seal of the Lotus Family.
Following the preceding heart-mudrā of the Buddha Family,
bend the left thumb into the palm;
the right thumb, as before, is held upright, and the mudrā is thus formed.
This is called the Heart-Seal Mantra of the Lotus Family, which is as follows:
Oṃ aruli. Next, one should bind the Samaya Seal of the Vajra Family, following the same procedure as the Heart Seal of the Buddha Family.
Insert the right thumb into the palm and extend the left thumb straight upward; this constitutes [the mudrā].
This is called the Heart Mudrā of the Vajra Family. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vajra-dhṛk. Next, form the armor mudrā:
interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward;
extend the two middle fingers and bend their upper joints so that they resemble the shape of a sword.
Place the tips of both index fingers against the backs of the middle fingers.
With this mudrā, empower the five locations—the forehead, right shoulder, left shoulder, heart, and throat—once while reciting the mantra:
Oṃ cakravartī prasamitāra-dara-dara vāsacarusniṣa-rukṣa-rukṣa-ma hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Next, form the Buddha-eye (Buddhalocanā) mudrā.
Join the two hands in *añjali*;
bend the two index fingers so that they each rest against the backs of the middle fingers;
then, bend both thumbs together and insert them into the palms.
The mantra for empowering the five places with the mudrā is as follows:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānām | oṃ ruru saparu jvala tiṣṭha siddhalocane sarvārthasādhanī svāhā*. Next, form the Great Ocean Mudrā (*mahāsāgaramudrā*).
Interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward,
join the palms together,
and spread the two thumbs apart.
Seal [the area] by circling it three times to the right.
Visualize the mantra for the great ocean water as:
Oṃ vimalodake svāhā. Next, within that great ocean, visualize Mount Sumeru, composed of the four jewels.
Interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward;
clench them tightly into fists,
join the wrists, and extend the fingers upward together.
Then the mantra is recited:
Oṃ ajara hūṃ. Next, upon the summit of Mount Sumeru, one should visualize a pavilion made of the seven precious jewels.
Then, one should form the seal of the Adhiṣṭhita Ratnakūṭāgāra.
With the two hands joined in the vajra-añjali, the first phalanges of each of the ten fingers on the left and right are interlaced; this constitutes the true mantra as follows:
*Namo samantabuddhānām. Oṃ svatāḥ uṣṇīṣate saparākṣama gagaṇe svāhā.* Next, bind the seal of the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa Cakravartin.
Interlace the two hands within to form fists;
extend the two middle fingers, bending their upper joints into the shape of swords,
and extend the two thumbs side by side.
Bend the two middle fingers and press their tips against the heads of the two thumbs;
thus the mudrā is formed.
The mantra for the protection of the five places is as follows:
*Namo samantabuddhānām* *būruṃ*. Next, form the mudrā of the net-stake (*vāraṇakīla*), following the previous root mudrā;
bend the upper joints of both index fingers.
Do not let the backs touch.
Press each of the two thumbs against the upper and lower parts respectively;
by swinging and rotating them, the knots are formed. The mantra for binding the upper and lower boundaries is as follows:
Namo samantabuddhānām | apratihataśāsanānām | Oṃ vighnāntaka sani kapi raivariṇi trāsaya vajravega sādya nṛtya vanaṃ sthara ruṣkhaṃ maḥ | Next, perform the mudrā for binding the boundary wall.
Following the previous root mudrā,
bend the two index fingers so that their two joints press against each other,
and hold the two thumbs upright and flat.
Attach the two index fingers and rotate them three times to the right; this constitutes the Vajra-Wall Boundary Mantra, which is:
*Oṃ* (prolonged), *maho*, *namas* (as before). Next, form the chariot mudrā (*ratha-mudrā*).
Interlace the two hands with palms facing upward;
extend the two index fingers so that their nails touch side by side;
and bend the two thumbs so that each rests beneath the base of its respective index finger.
Visualize [the deity] in another world.
The mantra for welcoming the Honored One is:
Oṃ tura tura hūṃ. Next, perform the mudrā for welcoming the chariot.
Following the previous seal for the chariot,
extend the tips of both thumbs toward the middle fingers and beckon three times toward oneself; the mantra is as follows:
*Namo siddhyeḥ ṭivikānaṃ tathāgatānām | Oṃ vajrīṇi yakṣaye svāhā.* If one is dismissing [the deities], recite *yakṣa-karṣaya*. Next, form the mudrā for invitation.
Following the previous root mudrā,
bend the right index finger behind the middle finger and perform three beckoning gestures forward; the mantra is as follows:

*Namo bhagavate aparājita-śriye | ehe ehi bhagavan dharma-rāja-praticchedaka-nagna-gandha-puṣpa-dhūpa-mālā-vastra-bilvākṣa-aparājita-mālā-prakrama-svāhā.* Next, one should form the *Sarvakarmakarī-Uṣṇīṣa-mudrā*.
Interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward.
Extend the two middle fingers and bend their upper joints into the shape of a sword.
This mantra is used for all offering substances, as well as for bathing water, cleansing earth, and so forth.
This mantra is used for empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*), expulsion (*vidhūnana*), removal of defilements, and boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*).
For expulsion, one turns [the hands] counter-clockwise; for boundary-binding, one turns them clockwise. The mantra is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ oṃ dhuru oṃ maṇḍa svāhā*. Next, perform again the seal of the previous net and stake (*kīla*).
First, use it to bind the boundary above.
Next, perform the seal of Aśvamukhī (Horse-faced One):
extend both hands with the left covering the right.
By erecting the two thumbs, it is accomplished.
Turning once to the right, one forms the *guhyasīvana* (secret-sewing) mudrā;
the mantra is: Oṃ asaṃjñini hūṃ phaṭ. Next, one binds the *argha* offering mudrā.
Following the previous root mudrā,
bend both index fingers so that they each rest against the middle fingers,
and extend both thumbs upright.
The mantra for each, attached to the side of the base of the index finger, is as follows:
*Namo samantabuddhānām oṃ ākarṣaya ākarṣaṇapratīccha amukaṃ svāhā*. Next, re-bind the fundamental mudrā.
Next, perform the mudrā for offering the lion throne.
This follows the previous root mudrā,
with the exception that the two index fingers are bent against the sides of the two thumbs.
The mantra is:
Oṃ ajara-vīrya svāhā. Next, form the incense mudrā, following the previous root mudrā.
Bend the right index finger and rest it upon the lower joint of the left middle finger. The mantra is:
*Namo samanta-buddhānām oṃ tāḍa lu-kye jñāna-te hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā*. Next, perform the mudrā for offering flowers.
Following the previous method for the incense-mark mudrā,
change the left index finger so that it rests against the lower joint of the left middle finger. The mantra is as follows:
Namo samanta-buddhānām | Oṃ sarvaloka-puṣpa-pūjāye hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā | Next, perform the incense mudrā.
Following the previous root mudrā, bend both index fingers so that they each rest against the middle joints of the middle fingers. The mantra is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ oṃ vīragata-vīrata-durbhaya hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā*. Next, form the food-offering mudrā (*naivedya-mudrā*).
Following the previous fundamental mudrā,
bend the upper joints of both index fingers so that they each rest against the side of the thumbs. The mantra is as follows:
Namo samantabuddhānām | Oṃ sarvalokamari-priye hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā | Next, bind the mudrā for offering lamps.
Following the previous root mudrā,
bend the two index fingers at their second joints so that they do not touch one another.
Place both thumbs upon the index fingers. The mantra is:

*Namo samantabuddhānām oṃ sarvaloka-saṃdarśana hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā*. Next, form the seal for universal offering and empowerment: join the palms with the hollows facing upward and place them on the crown of the head, crossing the two middle joints of each finger. The mantra is: [as above].
*Namo samantabuddhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ oṃ sarvatrāsaṅgasumitāvikira śāntinamostute svāhā.* Next, form the seal of the *Samantaprabha-buddhoṣṇīṣa*.
Interlace the two hands within,
forming fists,
and cause the joints of the two middle fingers to rise slightly.
The mantra is:
Namaḥ samantabuddhānām, amoḥ. Next, form the mudrā of Sitātapatrā-uṣṇīṣa with the two thumbs.
Twist the upper sides of the two ring fingers against each other;
join the tips of the two index fingers and bend them into the shape of a lid;
slightly bend and join the two middle fingers.
With the two little fingers extended upward and joined together, the mantra is:
*Namo samantabuddhānām apratihataśāsanānām oṃ mama maṃ hūṃ ṭiṭṭi*. Next, form the seal of the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa Radiant Mass (*Prabhāsa-ghana-uṣṇīṣa*).
Following the previous *Sitātapatrā-mudrā*, separate the two index fingers; this constitutes the mantra:

*Namo samantabuddhānām aparājitāśasanānām | Oṃ tathāgatadhvajāgravatīruciraśi hūṃ jvala jvala dhaka dhaka nara nara vinara vinara cchinda cchinda bhinda bhinda hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā* Next, form the *Uṣṇīṣavijayā-mudrā*.
Following the previous *Sitātapatrā* mudrā,
bend the two index fingers so that each rests upon the back of the middle phalanx of its respective middle finger.
The mantra is:
*Namo samantabuddhānām apratihataśāsanānām oṃ jvālajvāla bhīṣaṇa agnituṣṇīṣa hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā*. Next, bind the seal of the Supreme Buddha-uṣṇīṣa.
Form the Uṣṇīṣa-mudrā as before;
move the two index fingers upward about the distance of two barley grains. The mantra is: [mantra].
Namo samantabuddhānām apratihataśāsanānām | Oṃ jvalarañjuśriye hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Next, bind the seal of the Vajra-destroying Buddha-uṣṇīṣa (Vijirāṇa).
Interlace the two hands within to form fists;
extend the two middle fingers and bend their joints,
placing the tip of the right middle finger against the surface of the left middle finger.
To cause [the obstruction] to emerge to the extent of half a joint, the mantra is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānām apratihataśāsānām oṃ vikiraṇa dhuna dhuna duk*. Next, perform the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa mudrā of binding and crushing.
Following the previous procedure, change the left middle finger so that it touches the surface of the right middle finger,
leaving a space of about half a joint; the mantra is as follows:
*Namo samantabuddhānām apratihataśāsanānām | Oṃ apratihata-uṣṇīṣāya sarvavighnavināśanakarāya trātāya svāhā.* Next, bind the heart-seal of the Cakravartin-Uṣṇīṣa.
Following the previous root mudrā, bend both index fingers so that they each rest upon the upper joint of the middle fingers. The mantra is as follows:

Namo samanta-buddhānām apratihata-śāsānām | Oṃ tathāgatoṣṇīṣānavarocita-buddhni-karavarti hūṃ jvala jvala dhaka dhaka duna viduna trāsaya māraya uccāṭaya ha ha ha ha bhañja bhañja amṛte kumbhini kuṇḍaliṇi apratihatā-sattva-dhāriṇi hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Next, bind the heart-of-the-heart mudrā.
Following the previous root mudrā, bend both index fingers and place them respectively upon the upper joints of the two middle fingers. The mantra is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānām apratihataśāsanānām oṃ apratihata-tathāgata-*. For the Universal Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa Mudrā: with both hands, form the hollowed vajra-palms.
It is as if flowers were held in the palm of one's hand.
If a practitioner is in haste and unable to perform all the various Buddha-uṣṇīṣa mudrās,
they need only form this mudrā and recite the mantras of the various Buddha-uṣṇīṣas.
Next, bind the crown mudrā.
It is modeled after the previous root mudrā;
bend the right index finger.
Place them behind the right middle finger so that they do not touch; the mantra is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānām apratihataśāsānām oṃ khaṅkara-vajri oṃ hūṃ*. Next, perform the head mudrā.
Following the previous root mudrā, extend both index fingers straight upward behind the middle fingers so that they do not touch, slightly bending them.
The mantra for this is the same as above: "I take refuge... (Namo).
Oṃ kṣaravarti hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Next, again form the root mudrā.
Next, form the Great Samaya Mudrā.
For the empowerment of the *iṣṭadevatā*, interlace the two hands with palms facing inward,
extend the two middle fingers,
and bend the two index fingers behind the middle fingers.
With the hooks separated by the distance of a single barley grain,
place both thumbs against the base of the index fingers and rotate them three times to the right; the mantra is as follows:
Oṃ Śaṅkara Mahāsamayina Svāhā. Next, recite the hymn of one hundred and eight names.
When wishing to perform the recitation, first establish oneself as the principal deity through the five limbs (*pañcāṅga*).
Alternatively, one may accomplish the yoga of the principal deity through the five aspects;
or, at the three locations— the crown of the head, the tongue, and the heart— one visualizes the single-syllable Uṣṇīṣa,
thereby accomplishing the principal deity seated upon an eight-petaled lotus.
One should visualize the seven treasures upon each and every petal;
however, one should specifically visualize the Honored One Locanā upon the front petal of the lotus.
Next, one should hold the jewel, as described in the sūtra spoken at the site of the Bodhi-maṇḍala.
Next, holding the rosary with palms joined and supporting the rosary, recite the Mantra for Purifying the Rosary seven times. The mantra is:
Oṃ ānubuddhe-vijaye siddhisiddhārthe svāhā. Next, perform the mudrā for holding the rosary.
With the thumbs of both hands,
press down upon the nails of the ring fingers;
keep the two middle fingers and the two little fingers straight and upright.
Bend the two index fingers behind the middle fingers so that they do not touch,
forming the half-vajra mudrā as in the Vairocanābhisaṃbodhi Sūtra.
The mantra is:
Next, one should purify the mind; recite the mantra according to the Dharma while holding the rosary at the heart.
Fixing the mind on the tip of the nose, pronounce the syllables clearly—neither too slowly nor too hurriedly.
Yawning, belching, coughing, spitting, nasal mucus, and the like,
when associated with the mind, as well as mental focus on painful sensations—
such faults as these will all prevent accomplishment.
While reciting, one must not allow the body or mind to become weary or indolent.
If fatigue arises, one should immediately form the mudrā of the five offerings.
Recite the praises and offer the argha water while maintaining mindfulness.
Upon finishing the recitation, place the rosary upon the crown of your head.
Next, form the previously mentioned mudrā of the secret seam and rotate it once counter-clockwise.
This immediately constitutes the delimitation of the boundary (*sīmābandha*).
Next, perform the seal for the respectful dismissal (*visarjana-mudrā*),
following the previous root seal (*mūla-mudrā*).
Throw the left index finger outward and recite the invocation mantra *cchyi cchyi*,
adding the words *kaca kaca*.
This completes the act of respectful offering.
Next, one should again form the mudrās for the wall, the net, the stakes, and so forth,
to provide protection for the site above and below, as well as for the objects to be accomplished.
Next, perform the Kīlikī mudrā:
press the left thumb over the nail of the left little finger,
and spread the tips of the remaining three fingers apart.
Hold it upright like the shape of a three-pronged vajra.
Rotate it to the right three times; the mantra for forming the boundary (*sīmābandha*) is:
Oṃ kili kili vajra hūṃ phaṭ. Next, form the Muṇḍarī mudrā.
Cross the two little fingers within the palms;
place the two ring fingers over the little fingers,
and press down upon the two ring fingers with the two thumbs.
Join the two middle fingers together.
Bend the two index fingers behind the middle fingers so that they are separated by the distance of a single grain of barley.
Rotate clockwise three times; this constitutes the mantra for binding the boundary (*sīmābandha*). The mantra is as follows:
From the one-syllable mantra up to the fifteen-syllable mantra, calculate according to the number of syllables: for ten syllables, one lakṣa;
and so on, down to three syllables, where one should recite three lakṣas.
The Ritual for Reciting the One-Syllable Cakravartin King:
One Scroll; for those with thirty characters or more, one should recite ten thousand times.
